rule: Do not add new email-related configuration options to airflow-core; route all email settings through the SMTP provider.
trigger: A new config key referencing email, SMTP, or a notifier default is added inside airflow-core/src/airflow/config_templates/config.yml
rationale: The community agreed to migrate all email integration out of core into the SMTP provider; adding new core email config options contradicts that ongoing migration.

evidence.excerpt: We need to complete the Core->SMTP migration and deprecate all email related stuff

rule: Do not define domain-model enums (e.g. WeightRule) inside configuration.py; place them in the module that owns the concept.
trigger: A class definition for an Enum or domain type is added to airflow-core/src/airflow/configuration.py
rationale: configuration.py is for config parsing; domain enums placed there mislead readers about where the concept lives and create unusual coupling.

evidence.excerpt: it looks like a very odd location to put this enum

rule: Expose internal collections from AirflowConfigParser via methods returning immutable sequences (tuple), not as mutable-list properties.
trigger: A @property in AirflowConfigParser or a subclass returns a mutable list[...] type annotation
rationale: Mutable list properties on the config object are brittle; callers can mutate the internal state unexpectedly. Returning a tuple from a method makes the contract explicit.

evidence.excerpt: Return a tuple from a method. Hidden, mutable lists as a property are brittle.

rule: Use `tuple[DagWarningType, ...]` (open-ended homogeneous tuple) for warning_types parameters to avoid breaking callers when new warning types are added.
trigger: A function parameter typed tuple[DagWarningType, DagWarningType] (fixed-length) is added or modified in dag_processing/collection.py
rationale: Using a fixed-length tuple type forces a signature change whenever a new DagWarningType is added; the open-ended form avoids that churn.

evidence.excerpt: use this everywhere for warning_types so we can avoid signature change in the future

rule: When removing a parameter from DagBag or DagBag.collect_dags, either drop it entirely from the signature and docstring, or emit a UserWarning when it is supplied, rather than silently ignoring it.
trigger: A parameter of DagBag.__init__ or DagBag.collect_dags is removed from the implementation body but kept in the function signature or docstring
rationale: Silently ignoring a still-documented parameter is a footgun for CLI commands and tests that pass the argument expecting an effect.

evidence.excerpt: silently ignoring a still-documented bool is a real footgun for anyone writing CLI commands

rule: In DagBundleManager._refresh_dag_bundles, only remove a bundle from _force_refresh_bundles after DB persistence succeeds, and clear _bundle_versions on persistence failure to prevent stale-version short-circuiting.
trigger: Code removes a bundle from _force_refresh_bundles before the corresponding update_bundle_state call, or swallows an exception from update_bundle_state without clearing _bundle_versions
rationale: On persistence failure the cached version prevents other processors from detecting the new bundle version for up to refresh_interval, leaving the DB stale.

rule: Do not rely on SQLAlchemy UPDATE rowcount==0 to detect a missing row across all supported databases; use an explicit SELECT/EXISTS check instead.
trigger: Code does `if result.rowcount == 0: raise` after a SQLAlchemy update() call on a single-row update
rationale: MySQL can report rowcount==0 for a no-op UPDATE on an existing row, causing a spurious RuntimeError and noisy logs.

evidence.excerpt: MySQL can report 0 when the row exists but the UPDATE is a no-op

rule: Docstrings on overridable DAG-processing methods must document no-op conditions explicitly so subclass authors understand inherited skip behaviour.
trigger: A public or protected method in dag_processing/ is decorated for override (or its docstring says 'override') but the docstring omits the conditions under which the default implementation is a no-op
rationale: An override author reading only the docstring may implement the wrong behaviour when the base silently skips work under certain conditions (e.g. unversioned bundles).

evidence.excerpt: an override author reading only the docstring may not realize they inherit the skip-when-unversioned behavior

rule: In dag_processing exception handlers that catch broad Exception, ensure CallbackBundleUnavailable (or other purpose-built sentinel exceptions) is not re-wrapped; let it propagate or explicitly re-raise.
trigger: An `except Exception` block in dag_processing/ wraps or swallows a re-raise that could originate from CallbackBundleUnavailable
rationale: Catching CallbackBundleUnavailable inside a broad handler loses the original reason, making debugging difficult and masking intentional skip signals.

evidence.excerpt: re-wraps with the generic message, losing the original reason

rule: In DagFileProcessorProcess, pass dag_file.rel_path from the DagFileInfo object directly rather than recomputing it with Path.relative_to().
trigger: Code inside dag_processing/processor.py calls Path(path).relative_to(bundle_path) when a DagFileInfo object with a rel_path attribute is already available in the call chain
rationale: Path.relative_to() raises ValueError if the path is outside bundle_path (e.g. via symlink resolution); the already-computed rel_path on DagFileInfo is safer.

evidence.excerpt: relative_to will raise ValueError if path ever drifts outside bundle_path

rule: Example DAGs that fix timezone-related bugs must include a regression test that imports the DAG with a non-UTC default_timezone (e.g., Asia/Shanghai) to prevent OverflowError recurrence.
trigger: A commit modifies an example_dags/ file to fix a datetime/timezone issue but adds no test exercising a non-UTC [core] default_timezone
rationale: The existing test suite only exercises UTC; non-UTC timezone configurations expose OverflowError in datetime arithmetic that goes undetected without an explicit regression test.

evidence.excerpt: Adding a regression test that imports this file with a non-UTC timezone

rule: In BaseExecutor.run_workload() and related executor entry-points, guard setproctitle usage with a macOS (darwin) platform check.
trigger: Code in airflow-core/src/airflow/executors/ calls setproctitle() without a `sys.platform != 'darwin'` (or equivalent) guard
rationale: Other executor entry-points (LocalExecutor, Celery) already skip setproctitle on macOS to avoid known issues; omitting the guard from BaseExecutor reintroduces that problem.

evidence.excerpt: add the same darwin guard here to avoid reintroducing macOS issues

rule: New executor workload features must be implemented in BaseExecutor (or a shared mixin) so that each concrete executor does not need to be individually updated.
trigger: A new workload-handling method or branch is added to multiple concrete executor files (e.g., local_executor.py, celery_executor.py) without a corresponding base-class implementation
rationale: Requiring all executors to implement the same generic feature independently is unsustainable; the feature should live in the base class.

evidence.excerpt: all executors must be touched to implement this feature; would it be possible to use a base class?

rule: The executor workload type error message must be generated dynamically from the ExecutorWorkload union rather than by manually listing type names in an f-string.
trigger: An f-string in base_executor.py lists concrete workload type names (ExecuteTask, ExecuteCallback, TestConnection, …) manually rather than unpacking them from the type alias
rationale: Manually maintained lists go out of date when new workload types are added; deriving the list from the type union ensures the error is always accurate.

evidence.excerpt: generate this list by unpacking ExecutorWorkload instead of manually adding new workload types

rule: In prepare_file_queue, use the pre-built presence_key index dict to look up file stats in O(1) rather than performing an O(n) linear scan per file, avoiding O(n²) overall complexity.
trigger: Code in dag_processing/manager.py builds a dict keyed by file.presence_key but then calls a helper (e.g. processed_recently) that iterates over _file_stats linearly
rationale: prepare_file_queue is called on every scheduling loop cycle; O(n²) behaviour degrades heavily at scale.
